title: One interface across lessons
statement: Give every lesson in a course the same controls and components, so lessons differ in content and structure, not in how they work.
detail: Feedback on the reading course asked for interface standardization among other changes (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`). A later ruling required every other lesson to follow the reference lesson's interface to the tee, with no variations. A census of the page's interface classes confirmed that a rebuilt lesson differed, and the following lessons were rebuilt keeping their own structure while their components were made to look exactly like the reference's (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0222-g3-l4-l1-parity-rebuild-2026-09-17-to-21.qmd`).
against: The evidence is a ruling and the rebuild that followed it, not a measured effect on students.

evidence.quote: On all the other lessons, we have to follow the UI/UX to the tee — no variations at all.
A DOM-class census on main confirmed it
rule: our structure stays, his components look exactly like his
read live from its Lesson 1 so an exported lesson speaks in the build's own words.
Used only where the build's own lines cannot be read (no mirror): plain, and never the answer.
Plain lines of ours: who speaks, never the content.
One "Scout says" component would carry instruction, encouragement and feedback, and would give the app a single voice.
Both survived because they were not quite the same control, the bar holding whether narration autoplays and the pill playing this page, a distinction no child can see.

evidence.path: sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx
evidence.quote: The lesson shape is fixed: video, read with purpose, a block of tasks, the Modelling Moment, Part 3, closing, doors. Only the task block flexes.

UNIFORMITY against the reviewer-approved baseline lesson (stems, recaps, feedback voice, wrap shape, banners, silent-node reasons) — "what would a child feel as a DIFFERENT app". Procedure differences don't excuse voice differences.
The video player chrome is identical across lessons … This does not ban checkpoint-triggered content from varying
